newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Bank Handlowy accepts IPO price range.
newsitem.headline: Polish Bank Handlowy accepts IPO price range.

text.p: The president of Poland's Bank Handlowy SA said on Saturday that the bank, which had been involved in discussing the price range for its initial public offering, stood by the decision to put it at 28 to 35 zlotys ($10.92).

"As we were one of those who took part...according to certain assumptions we stand by this price," Cezary Stypulkowski told Reuters over the telephone but declined to comment on whether he considered the price level advantageous.
He said that the price decision, reached late on Friday by the Treasury ministry and its advisors after consultation with the bank, had taken standard factors into account.
"One looks at the market, at the position, at the fact that this is an initial public offering, at comparisons, at the need to assure the effectiveness of the offer," he said.
Bank officials said there would be a news conference at 11.00 a.m. (0900 GMT) on Monday, when Poland starts the sale.
Analysts had suggested a broad spectrum of likely prices ranging up to 45 or 50 zlotys and the proposed range appeared to be more towards the lower end of expectations.
Poland is offering 95 percent of Handlowy's 65 million shares in the privatisation scheme.
It is offering 19,500,000 shares in the institutional investor tranche and 9,750,000 shares in the individual investor tranche, for both of which main orders are to be placed from May 26.
The final price for the tranches will be set on June 17.
Retail investors will be allotted shares at a special bourse session on June 21.
A further 4,641,000 will go to employees.
A price for a 27,859,000 share tranche earmarked for a small group of selected investors will be set later in talks with these investors. -- Anthony Barker +48 22 653 9700 ($ = 3.202 Polish Zlotys)
